metadata.title: Quit or Laid Off? Who Ends Jobs
metadata.section: Section C: Labor Dynamics, Wages & Consumer Prices

events.label: Great Recession: 2.65 million layoffs in one month
COVID: record 13 million layoffs in one month
The Great Resignation: 4.45 million quit in one month

explanation.summary: Every month millions of Americans are hired, quit, or are laid off, while employers post millions of open jobs. These four flows show the health of the job market better than the unemployment rate alone. Many quits mean workers feel confident they can find something better.
explanation.methodology: Job openings, hires, quits and layoffs-and-discharges (levels, thousands, seasonally adjusted) from the BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS).

key_findings.title: 2009: The Job Market Freezes
key_findings.description: Openings fell to 2.23 million and hires to 3.64 million, the lowest on the chart. Quits dropped to 1.56 million: people held on to the jobs they had.
key_findings.significance: When nobody is hiring, nobody dares to quit.

key_findings.title: March 2020: 13 Million Layoffs
key_findings.description: Layoffs and discharges hit 12.99 million in a single month as COVID closed the economy. In normal months the number is about 1.5 to 2 million.
key_findings.significance: The largest one-month job loss in the record.

key_findings.title: 2022: The Great Resignation
key_findings.description: Openings reached a record 12.3 million in March 2022 and quits a record 4.50 million in April 2022. As of August 2026, openings are 7.1 million and quits 3.1 million.
key_findings.significance: Workers changed jobs for better pay at the fastest rate ever measured.
